title: Landlord or Tenant Works? A Newcastle Office Fitout Responsibility Checklist

body:
## Who is responsible for landlord and tenant fitout works?

For a Newcastle office fitout, the answer comes from the actual lease, works agreements, appointments and applicable requirements. Do not allocate a job simply because someone calls it a base-building item or a tenant improvement. Clarify what has been agreed and have unresolved legal and technical questions reviewed by the appropriate advisers.

The practical goal is a single schedule showing what will be delivered, who has agreed to arrange it, who pays, what it depends on and what evidence is needed at completion. A promise that the premises will be “ready” leaves too much room for different interpretations.

Your Office Space provides client-side project management. We help coordinate the agreed brief, budget, scope, programme and client decisions. YOS does not carry out fitout construction as principal contractor. Appointed contractors, designers, certifiers and other specialist advisers retain their respective responsibilities.

[BUTTON: Plan my Newcastle fitout responsibilities]

**Free working pack:** [Download the two-page works responsibility checklist (PDF)](/guides/landlord-tenant-fitout-works-newcastle-checklist.pdf) or [use the editable text version](/guides/landlord-tenant-fitout-works-newcastle-checklist.txt). Use it with your solicitor and appointed project team. It is a planning record, not a lease amendment or instruction to a contractor.

## Begin with the documents, not a default rule

Gather the proposed or signed lease, relevant works agreements, landlord fitout guide, condition records, current plans and written correspondence about promised works. Note the document and clause reference against each item, and ask your solicitor to resolve conflicts or missing terms.

The NSW Small Business Commission's [Retail Tenancy Guide](https://www.smallbusiness.nsw.gov.au/about-retail-leases/retail-tenancy-guide) explains that different laws cover retail, commercial and residential leases. Its retail provisions should not be assumed to govern every office tenancy. Ask your solicitor which regime and documents apply to the actual premises and business.

Use this article to prepare a clear discussion. It does not determine who is legally liable for a particular cost, what remedy is available for delay or whether a party has fulfilled its obligations.

## Separate six questions for every works item

| Question | What to record | Why it helps the project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What is being delivered? | Specific scope and relevant drawing or specification | Makes vague promises and gaps visible |
| Who arranges delivery? | Agreed party and appointed provider | Identifies who needs to act |
| Who pays? | Agreed payer, cost basis and unresolved amounts | Helps avoid omissions or double counting in the budget |
| What permissions and advice are needed? | Responsible adviser and required decisions | Connects the works to the approvals workstream |
| What must happen first? | Access, information and programme dependencies | Shows which other activities rely on the item |
| How is completion evidenced? | Required records and the authorised reviewer | Defines what needs to be checked before the next stage |

The same organisation need not answer every question. The person paying for an item may not be the person arranging it, and delivery does not automatically establish acceptance or certification. Record the actual agreement and appointments.

## Make building-services interfaces explicit

An existing air-conditioning system does not tell you whether it suits the proposed layout and use. Available power, data, fire systems, amenities and access can also require investigation. Ask the relevant specialists what information and assessments are needed; do not treat a marketing description as a capacity confirmation.

For each interface, ask where one scope ends and the next starts. Does the agreed scope cover an assessment only, a defined upgrade, connection to another party's work or completion records? Who coordinates the information between providers? Mark unanswered items as unresolved rather than assigning them by assumption.

Use the [Newcastle fitout readiness guide](/blog/office-fitout-readiness-newcastle) to gather the premises questions, then transfer the agreed delivery items into this works schedule. The [approvals guide](/blog/office-fitout-approvals-newcastle) helps keep property consent and statutory questions separate.

## Describe landlord works in measurable terms

Instead of recording only “landlord to prepare the space”, ask for a defined scope supported by the relevant drawings, specification and written agreement. Include the proposed delivery date, access assumptions, evidence of completion and any matters requiring adviser confirmation.

A hypothetical example is a proposed meeting-room layout that relies on a services assessment being completed first. The useful record identifies who arranges that assessment, the information they need, when the result is required and who reviews its implications for the design. It does not assume that either landlord or tenant is automatically responsible.

Where the proposed lease or works terms need strengthening, have your solicitor advise on the wording and consequences. A project worksheet supports that conversation; it does not create an enforceable promise on its own.

[BUTTON: Discuss landlord and tenant works coordination]

## Connect access, completion and business dates

Place landlord and tenant activities on one coordinated programme. Ask which items must be finished before the next contractor can work, which inspections or decisions are needed and what affects furniture, IT and the intended move.

Have your solicitor clarify the lease consequences of access, commencement dates, incentives and delayed works. Do not assume that early access is rent-free, that it changes a lease date or that the business can occupy simply because a room looks finished.

If work must continue around trading, use the [staying-open refurbishment guide](/blog/office-refurbishment-newcastle-stay-open). A date on the programme needs supporting scope, information and access arrangements, not just a target opening day.

## Keep changes and end-of-lease questions visible

When an agreed item changes, record the proposed scope, cost and timing effects and obtain the required decisions under the relevant agreements. Keep the works schedule aligned with the current design and the [fitout change register](/blog/office-fitout-variations-newcastle).

Also ask who owns installed items, who maintains them and what the lease requires at the end of the term. Use the [make-good planning guide](/blog/make-good-obligations-commercial-lease-cost) to prepare questions for your solicitor and relevant advisers. A new fitout should not leave the end-of-lease assumptions undocumented.

## Newcastle landlord and tenant works checklist

- Collect the lease, works agreements, fitout guide and condition records.
- Confirm the applicable lease framework with your solicitor.
- Describe each works item with a document reference.
- Record who has agreed to arrange delivery.
- Record the agreed payer and cost basis separately.
- Mark unallocated scope and unpriced items as unresolved.
- Allocate services investigations to appropriately appointed specialists.
- Record permissions, access and information dependencies.
- Link the works dates to the wider programme.
- Identify completion evidence and the authorised reviewer.
- Record changes against the current scope revision.
- Obtain advice on ownership, maintenance and make-good requirements.

## Coordinate the fitout from the client's side

YOS can help keep the agreed works scope, budget interfaces and client decisions visible under a defined client-side engagement. We work with the relevant parties to track information and programme dependencies; the appointed contractors perform the construction and specialists provide their respective advice.

[Explore YOS Newcastle office fitout project management](/office-fitout). If the premises decision is still being negotiated, our [tenant representation service](/tenant-rep) may also be relevant under a separate agreed scope.

Tell us the suburb, project stage, works promised, documents available and target move date. We can discuss what needs organising next.

[BUTTON: Get help coordinating my fitout works]

## Common questions

### Does the landlord always pay for base-building upgrades?

Do not assume an allocation from that label. The lease, works agreements, actual scope and applicable requirements need review. Ask your solicitor and relevant technical advisers to confirm responsibilities for the project.

### Is a landlord works schedule enough to change the lease?

A planning worksheet does not amend a lease or works agreement. Have your solicitor advise on the documents, wording and approvals needed to record enforceable obligations.

### Can we start our fitout before the landlord works finish?

That depends on the works, access, approvals, appointments and the responsible team’s assessment of the sequence. Confirm the actual dependencies and legal arrangements before committing to a start date.

### How does YOS help with landlord and tenant works?

Under an agreed client-side engagement, YOS can help organise the scope schedule, information, budget interfaces and decisions across the programme. YOS does not replace the solicitor, principal contractor, designer or certifier.
